sources.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
facts_adopted: Repository maps, product behavior, logs, metrics, traces, mechanical constraints, and entropy control are parts of an agent harness.
sources.limits: First-party engineering practice, not proof of this product or a prescribed command topology.

sources.title: Follow a goal
facts_adopted: Durable goals need a clear outcome, constraints, stop condition, validation loop, and checkpoint controls.
sources.limits: Platform goal state must be observed through the platform and cannot be inferred from repository receipts.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.6
facts_adopted: GPT-5.6 Sol is presented as a flagship coding model and Ultra as a multi-agent coordination mode.
sources.limits: Availability, active runtime metadata, worker count, and reasoning setting must be observed; none is a product correctness condition.

sources.title: Subagents
facts_adopted: Read-heavy work is safer to parallelize; write-heavy work risks conflict; the main agent integrates delegated results.
sources.limits: Product safety classes and acceptance rules are Harness-owned translations.

sources.title: Open-sourcing Symphony: building an orchestration layer for Codex
facts_adopted: Task/workspace dependencies are useful, but rigid state machines can constrain capable agents; objectives and tools enable adaptive execution.
sources.limits: Symphony is a design input, not a required dependency or architecture clone.

sources.title: Build skills
facts_adopted: Skills use progressive disclosure: concise discovery metadata first and complete selected instructions when invoked.
sources.limits: Current host context guidance is drift-prone and must be refreshed before release.

sources.title: Build plugins
facts_adopted: Plugins may bundle skills and MCP/app capabilities; marketplace, install, restart/discovery, and new-task testing are separate operational steps.
sources.limits: Exact host paths and behavior are versioned product surfaces and require live verification.

sources.title: Building self-improving tax agents with Codex
facts_adopted: Production evidence and corrections can be turned into findings, evaluations, and scoped improvement tasks.
sources.limits: Domain-specific results do not prove general autonomous self-improvement.

sources.title: Separating signal from noise in coding evaluations
facts_adopted: Coding evaluation tasks can be broken by overly strict tests, underspecified prompts, low-coverage tests, or misleading setup; evaluation data needs quality review.
sources.limits: Reported benchmark proportions are not generalized as a Harness product rate.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
facts_adopted: Stronger agent autonomy does not remove the need to preserve scope, permissions, and safety boundaries.
sources.limits: System-level safety evaluation is not product-specific security proof.

sources.title: Monitoring Distributed Systems
facts_adopted: Latency, traffic, errors, and saturation are key signals; dashboards, ad hoc analysis, trends, and simple robust alerts serve distinct purposes.
sources.limits: Service monitoring practices are translated to local agent/product operations rather than copied literally.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions
facts_adopted: Telemetry should use stable semantic names and types with explicit stability and evolution.
sources.limits: Harness-specific attributes require product prototyping and governance.

sources.title: How to write semantic conventions
facts_adopted: Conventions should be prototyped, clearly typed, and designed to avoid unstable or unbounded attributes.
sources.limits: Convention stability does not prove exporter or backend behavior.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Baggage
facts_adopted: Baggage has no built-in integrity and may propagate to downstream or third-party systems.
sources.limits: Implementation-specific propagation behavior still requires tests.

sources.title: Cargo Build Cache
facts_adopted: Cargo provides incremental/build cache substrate with defined inputs and locations.
sources.limits: Cargo cache validity does not establish Harness product cache or claim semantics.

sources.title: External Tools and Cargo JSON Messages
facts_adopted: Cargo exposes machine-readable build information suitable for external tooling.
sources.limits: Harness must still validate candidate identity and semantic affected closure.

sources.title: cargo-nextest documentation
facts_adopted: Nextest provides test listing, partitioning, retries policy, archives, and execution substrate.
sources.limits: It does not determine Harness impacted-test legality or fixture claim authority.

sources.title: Instrumenting your Rust code for code coverage
facts_adopted: Rustc supports source-based coverage instrumentation and profile generation.
sources.limits: Instrumentation output requires scoped collection, mapping, exclusion review, and candidate reconciliation.

sources.title: cargo-llvm-cov
facts_adopted: cargo-llvm-cov integrates Rust coverage collection, reports, and nextest workflows, with documented cleaning/profile caveats.
sources.limits: Third-party tool output is observation; Harness owns semantic coverage and claim guards.

sources.title: clap crate documentation
facts_adopted: Clap provides maintained command parsing, derive-based schemas, enums, help, and validation substrate.
sources.limits: Specific adoption is advisory pending dependency/build/UX measurement.

sources.title: Command Line Applications in Rust
facts_adopted: Predictable output, errors, exit status, and composability are core CLI usability practices.
sources.limits: Advisory practice, translated into product-specific behavioral requirements.

sources.title: SLSA v1.2 Provenance
facts_adopted: Artifact provenance should identify inputs, build process, and produced subject identity.
sources.limits: Provenance proves an integrity relationship, not product behavior.

sources.title: SLSA v1.2 Build Requirements
facts_adopted: Build isolation, parameter integrity, and cache-poisoning boundaries matter to artifact trust.
sources.limits: Local development may use lower assurance with an explicit ceiling; release claims require named level and proof.

sources.title: Cosign signing and verification documentation
facts_adopted: Signed bundles can bind release artifact identity to verification material.
sources.limits: Optional release control; signature validity cannot prove installation, discovery, or runtime behavior.

sources.title: Harness Ultragoal repository observation
facts_adopted: Current authority is duplicated across commands, manifests, matrices, fixtures, receipts, and historical lanes; plugin journeys lack one reconciled closure.
sources.limits: Snapshot is current only for the authoring context; live implementation must re-inventory.

Host plugin discovery can be verified through a stable API rather than UI automation.
